\section*{Responsible NLP Research Checklist}

% ARR Responsible NLP Research Checklist (2025/2026).
% Does not count toward the page limit.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.}]

%% A %%
\item \textbf{Did you describe the limitations of your work?}

Yes. A dedicated \emph{Limitations} section (after \S\ref{sec:discussion}) discusses: single-environment scope, death-penalty sensitivity, excluded task types, baseline strength, episode-level label granularity, and distribution shift.

%% B %%
\item \textbf{Did you discuss any potential risks of your work?}

Yes. The \emph{Ethics Statement} notes that the framework is a diagnostic analysis tool operating on publicly available benchmarks and models, with no direct negative societal impacts.

%% C %%
\item \textbf{Do the abstract and introduction summarize the paper's main claims?}

Yes. Both sections state the three core findings: (1) death avoidance is the dominant routing signal, (2) episode-level counterfactual labels expose this signal, and (3) current implicit routers cannot generalize it to unseen episodes.

\end{enumerate}

\bigskip\noindent
\textit{For the remaining questions, answer ``Yes'' only if the relevant justification or discussion is provided in the paper.}

\paragraph{D. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?}
Yes.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{D\arabic*.}]
\item \textbf{Did you cite the creators of artifacts you used?}\\
Yes. All benchmarks (ScienceWorld, ALFWorld, MATH) and models (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-it) are cited in \S\ref{sec:experiments} and the bibliography.

\item \textbf{Did you discuss the license or terms for use of artifacts?}\\
Yes. All benchmarks and models are publicly available under permissive licenses (Apache 2.0, MIT, or equivalent). This is noted in the Ethics Statement.

\item \textbf{Did you discuss if your use of existing artifact(s) is consistent with their intended use?}\\
Yes. Benchmarks are used for their intended purpose of evaluating agent capabilities; models are used for inference in evaluation settings.

\item \textbf{Did you discuss the steps taken to check whether the data contains any information that names or uniquely identifies individual people or offensive content?}\\
N/A. All data are synthetically generated trajectories from simulated environments (ScienceWorld, ALFWorld) or mathematical problems (MATH). No personal or offensive content is involved.

\item \textbf{Did you provide documentation of the artifacts?}\\
Yes. Experimental setup (\S\ref{sec:experiments}) documents environment configurations, model versions, and evaluation protocols. Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{E. Computational experiments.}
Yes, the paper includes computational experiments.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{E\arabic*.}]
\item \textbf{Did you report the number of parameters in the models used?}\\
Yes. Model sizes are specified: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B-it, Qwen2.5-72B for backbone agents; Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B for routers (Appendix~\ref{app:ablations}).

\item \textbf{Did you report the number of training and evaluation examples?}\\
Yes. Episode counts are reported per environment: 245 episodes for ScienceWorld pilot (\S\ref{sec:experiments}), with per-task breakdowns in Appendix~\ref{app:per-task}. Cross-environment and cross-model sample sizes are reported in \S\ref{sec:cross-env} and Appendix~\ref{app:cross-model}.

\item \textbf{Did you use evaluation metrics with a description and justification?}\\
Yes. Balanced accuracy (step-level and episode-level), death rates, and mean scores are defined and motivated in \S\ref{sec:experiments}. The Death Avoidance Fraction (DAF) metric is formally introduced in \S\ref{sec:daf}.

\item \textbf{Did you state whether you use existing packages?}\\
Yes. The paper uses HuggingFace Transformers, PyTorch, and standard scientific Python libraries. Router training uses the Transformers Trainer API.

\item \textbf{Is your evaluation done in a reproducible way?}\\
Yes. Random seeds are reported (4 seeds per router configuration), environment versions are specified, and all experiments use deterministic episode sampling. Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{F. Did you use or collect data from human participants?}
No. All data are generated from automated agent--environment interactions. No human annotation, evaluation, or data collection was conducted.

\paragraph{G. Did you use AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot) in the research process?}
Yes. AI assistants were used for code development and paper drafting. All generated content was reviewed and verified by the authors. The assistants were not used to generate experimental results or scientific claims.

\paragraph{H. Computational budget and environmental impact.}
Total estimated compute: approximately 300--400 GPU-hours across all experiments (data collection, router training, evaluation, and ablations). Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32\,GB) $\times$ 2 and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 $\times$ 4. Estimated carbon footprint: $\sim$40--55\,kg CO$_2$eq, based on a carbon intensity of $\sim$0.4\,kg CO$_2$/kWh and average GPU power draw of 300--350W. This estimate is approximate and depends on local grid carbon intensity.
TEXEOF
